title: Assembly overlay: the user's additions to a generated baseline assembly
description: The persistence half of hot installation. The product's baseline assembly is generated at startup; this document — living in the user directory (default ~/.lattice/assembly.json) — carries what the user had installed on top: extra components, extra instances, extra wires. Installs write it, startup merges it, so an installed component survives a restart. One document, many pens: installers append programmatically, the user may edit by hand. Each carried component manifest is additionally validated against schemas/component_manifest.json; the instances/wires shape against schemas/assembly_manifest.json. The merge is atomic: an overlay with any problem is skipped whole (with an explanation) rather than half-applied.

components.description: Component manifests (self-descriptions) the baseline registry does not have; each must satisfy the component-manifest canon

requires.description: Optional slot bound, same meaning as in the assembly manifest canon

instances.description: Instance name → which component, with what config; names must not collide with the baseline

wires.description: Extra wires; exact duplicates of baseline wires are dropped on merge (a doubled wire would mean doubled delivery)
